root_cause.text: In nfsd4_add_rdaccess_to_wrdeleg, the access count increment via __nfs4_file_get_access was performed unconditionally, even when the read file descriptor was already set by another thread, leading to an extra reference that prevents the nfsd_file from being freed.
root_cause.evidence: The patch moves __nfs4_file_get_access inside the `if (!fp->fi_fds[O_RDONLY])` block, and also moves the assignment of `fp->fi_rdeleg_file` inside that block to avoid a duplicate reference. The CVE description states: "if fp->fi_fds[O_RDONLY] is already set by another thread, __nfs4_file_get_access should not be called to increment the nfs4_file access count since that was already done by the thread that added READ access to the file."

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix reference counting and access accounting in nfsd4_add_rdaccess_to_wrdeleg by moving __nfs4_file_get_access and fi_rdeleg_file assignment inside the condition that allocates a new read-only file descriptor.
intent_record.what: Moved the calls to __nfs4_file_get_access and assignment to fp->fi_rdeleg_file from outside to inside the if block that checks if fp->fi_fds[O_RDONLY] is NULL.
intent_record.how: Now, __nfs4_file_get_access and nfsd_file_get for fi_rdeleg_file are only executed when the read-only file descriptor is newly allocated, preventing double-counting of access and leaking references when the fd already existed.

grouping_result.intent: Fix reference counting and access accounting in nfsd4_add_rdaccess_to_wrdeleg by moving __nfs4_file_get_access and fi_rdeleg_file assignment inside the condition that allocates a new read-only file descriptor.

relevance_review.reason: The group directly fixes the unconditional access count increment that caused the extra reference preventing nfsd_file from being freed, moving it inside the allocation condition as required.

candidates.rationale: This statement unconditionally increments the access count via __nfs4_file_get_access, even when the read file descriptor (fi_fds[O_RDONLY]) is already set by another thread. This extra reference prevents the nfsd_file from being freed, causing the vulnerability.

This statement unconditionally takes a reference to fi_rdeleg_file without considering whether a new file was allocated or one already existed. Combined with the unconditional access increment, it contributes to unbalanced reference counts, preventing file deallocation.
